To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed optimizations for managing uncertainties in power systems do not consider the extreme perturbances and their impacts are not evaluated properly.

(i) the risk of the large but rare blackouts should be assessed more carefully, and (ii) a variant of Monte-Carlo Simulation which considers the cascading and dependent outages can be used to evaluate the robustness and the resilience of the solutions of the optimizations for the management uncertainty.

the proposed optimizations in the literatures for managing uncertainties in power systems should consider the cascading outages and their effects on the system performance in the optimization problem in order to evaluate the value of risk properly.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the evaluation of risk and the response of the obtained solutions of proposed optimizations regarding robustness and resilience to the dependent and cascaded outages in order to assess the value of security in the power system operation.
the evaluation of the value of risk in the proposed optimizations of managing uncertainty in power systems.
the development of an effective approach for the evaluation of the value of risk of rare but large black-outs in power systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“the proposed optimization methods for managing uncertainty in power systems are not effective enough to evaluate the risk of the power systems in a reliable manner”.
the risk is evaluated effectively in the optimization approaches for the management of uncertainty in power systems.

there is a need to develop new optimization approaches which take into account the robustness and also resilience to both low-probability and low-impact as well as high-probability and high-impact perturbations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed optimizations are not capable of providing a tradeoff between robustness and resilience and the evaluation of the value of risk in these optimizations is not accurate.
the proposed optimization methods for the management of uncertainty in power systems are not effective in evaluating the risk and the value of risk.
the proposed optimization methods for the management of uncertainty in power systems do not consider the risk of extreme events properly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed optimizations should be evaluated carefully in terms of the risk and the obtained solutions should not be evaluated using a single measure of performance.
the proposed optimizations for managing uncertainties should be assessed in terms risk and not just in terms of robustness.
the risk of rare but large blackout events is not evaluated appropriately in the proposed optimization methods for the management of uncertainty in power systems.
